I'll tell you how the waiting for Jesus began. / / Long ago, in a small town called Nazareth, lived a young woman named Mary. Mary loved God very much. She sang little songs while she swept the floor, and she was kind to everyone she met. / / One day, Mary was home when the room filled up with a soft, shining light! And there stood an angel named Gabriel! Mary was very surprised. She held her hands to her heart. But the angel smiled kindly and said, "Do not be afraid, Mary! God is very happy with you!" / / Then the angel said, "You are going to have a baby boy, and you will name Him Jesus. He will be called the Son of God! He will be a king forever, and His kingdom will never end!" / / Mary was puzzled. She said, "How can this be?" And the angel told her, "Nothing is impossible with God!" The angel also told her a happy secret: her cousin Elizabeth, who was very old, was going to have a baby too! Mary smiled. God could do anything! / / Mary thought about it quietly. She wasn't scared anymore. She folded her hands and said, "I am the Lord's servant. Let it be just as you said." And she said yes to God, with a happy heart! Then the angel went back to heaven, and the room was quiet again. / / Soon, Mary went to visit her cousin Elizabeth. And when Elizabeth saw her, she cheered! Her baby jumped for joy inside her! Elizabeth said, "God has blessed you, Mary!" And Mary sang a happy song of thanks to God. "My soul is full of joy in God my Savior!" they sang together. / / So Eli, what do we learn? God keeps His promises! He sent His Son, Jesus, just as He said. And when God asks us to trust Him, we can say yes with a happy heart! Now let's sing "Yes, Mary Said Yes" together! Here we go!

33.script:
Hello, friends! Welcome back to Grandpa Sol's porch! Today Zara and Eli were waving green leaves in the air and marching around the porch, and Pip the lamb hopped along behind them. "Grandpa Sol, we are having a parade!" said Eli. Oh, how wonderful! Come sit down, my dears, and I will tell you about the happiest parade in the Bible.

Long ago, Jesus and His friends were walking toward the big city of Jerusalem. Jesus had helped so many people. He had made sick people well, and He had taught everyone about God's love. Now Jesus was going to Jerusalem, and many people were waiting to see Him.

When they came close to the city, Jesus said to two of His friends, "Go into the village ahead of you. You will find a young donkey tied there that no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it to Me. If anyone asks, just say, the Lord needs it."

The two friends went, and they found the donkey, just as Jesus said. They untied it and brought it to Jesus. They put their cloaks on the donkey's back, and Jesus sat down on it. A king rode a donkey, to show He came in peace, not to fight.

Then the people saw Jesus coming! They were so happy! Some people spread their cloaks on the road, like a soft, warm carpet. Other people cut green branches from the palm trees and laid them on the path. Children waved their branches high in the air.

And everyone shouted, "Hosanna! Hosanna! Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord!" Hosanna means, "Please save us!" The people knew that Jesus was God's own King, sent to save them. The whole road was full of singing and joy.

Jesus rode slowly through the happy crowd. He smiled at the children, and He waved to the people. He was not a king who wanted a big golden palace. He was a gentle king who came to love and to save.

Some people in the city were upset about all the cheering. But Jesus said, "Even the stones would cry out if the people stopped praising." Nothing could stop the praise that day!

So Zara, so Eli, what do we learn? Jesus is our gentle King, and we can praise Him with our whole hearts! Wave your leaves, my dears. Let's sing "Hosanna, Hosanna" together! Here we go!

34.script:
Hello, friends! Welcome back to Grandpa Sol's porch! Today Zara and Eli were carrying Pip the lamb in a blanket, like a little stretcher, and giggling. "Grandpa Sol, Pip is the one who needs help!" said Eli. Oh my, said Grandpa Sol with a smile, that reminds me of a story about four friends who carried someone they loved. Come sit close, my dears.

Long ago, Jesus was teaching in a house in a town called Capernaum. So many people came to hear Him that the house was full, and the doorway was full, and even outside was full. There was no room at all.

Now, in that town lived a man who could not walk. He lay on a mat all day, and he could not go anywhere by himself. But he had four good friends. They had heard that Jesus could help, and they said, "Let's take our friend to Jesus!"

The four friends picked up the mat, one on each corner, and carried their friend through the streets. But when they came to the house, they could not get in. The crowd was too big! Everyone was packed together like a basket of apples.

Did the friends give up? No! One of them said, "Look! We can go up on the roof!" In those days, roofs were flat, and people climbed up stairs outside the house. So the four friends carried the mat up, and up, and up to the roof.

Then they carefully made a hole in the roof, right over the place where Jesus was teaching. They lowered the mat slowly, down, down, down, on ropes. The people inside looked up in surprise, and bits of dust floated down!

Jesus looked up and saw the four friends and their great faith. He smiled. Then He looked at the man on the mat and said, "Friend, your sins are forgiven." And then Jesus said, "Get up, pick up your mat, and go home."

And do you know what happened? The man stood up! He picked up his mat and walked out, right in front of everybody! He was so happy, and he praised God. And the people were amazed and said, "We have never seen anything like this!"

So Zara, so Eli, what do we learn? Jesus is the best friend to bring our troubles to, and good friends help each other come to Jesus. Now let's sing "Bring Them to Jesus" together! Here we go!

35.script:
Hello, friends! Welcome back to Grandpa Sol's porch! Today Zara and Eli were holding a little basket of colored eggs, and Pip the lamb wore a tiny yellow ribbon. "Grandpa Sol, why is Easter so happy?" asked Zara. Ah, my dear, it is the happiest story of all. Come sit close, and I will tell you.

Long ago, Jesus died on a cross. His friends were very sad. They gently wrapped His body in clean cloth, and they laid Him in a stone tomb, a quiet cave cut into a hillside. Then a big, heavy stone was rolled in front of the door.

For two days, the friends cried and stayed close together. They did not know what would happen next. But Jesus had told them, "I will rise again on the third day."

Early on the third morning, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene and some other women walked to the tomb. They carried sweet-smelling spices. On the way they wondered, "Who will roll away the big stone for us?"

But when they came to the tomb, the stone was already rolled away! The tomb was open, and it was empty! Then two angels in shining clothes said, "Why are you looking for the living among the dead? He is not here. He is risen, just as He said!"

Mary stood outside the tomb, crying. Then she heard someone say, "Mary." She turned around, and it was Jesus! He was alive! Mary was so full of joy that she ran to tell the others, "I have seen the Lord!"

That same evening, Jesus came and stood with His friends, and He said, "Peace be with you." They were so happy! Jesus was truly alive, and He showed them that He had won over sin and death forever.

So Zara, so Eli, what do we learn? Jesus is alive! He loves us so much that He gave Himself for us, and now He lives forever. Easter is about Jesus. Now let's sing "He Is Alive" together! Here we go!
